newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA SCORE EIGHT TO GO TOP IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA SCORE EIGHT TO GO TOP IN SPAIN.

text.p: Hristo Stoichkov and Brazilian stars Ronaldo and Giovanni turned Barcelona's game with Logrones into a personal scoring battle as their side swept back to the top of the Spanish first division with an 8-0 win on Sunday.
With 20 points from eight games, Barcelona go two ahead of Real Madrid and Deportivo Coruna, after both sides scored comfortable wins on Saturday.
Reigning champions Atletico Madrid are already nine points off the pace after losing an exciting match 3-1 to Valencia.

Stoichkov, Ronaldo and Giovanni all scored twice as Barcelona romped home against a Logrones team that began the game unbeaten away from home and ended it with just nine players because of sendings-off.
An own goal and a strike by Juan Pizzi completed the account for Bobby Robson's side.
Barcelona had not won 8-0 since 1968, and the margin of victory could have been even greater but for Logrones keeper Andoni Cedrun.
"They massacred us...There are really big teams, and there are small ones, and money makes the difference." said Cedrun afterwards.
At one stage the fiery Stoichkov -- whose return to the Nou Camp has been overshadowed by Ronaldo's goalscoring feats -- had to wrestle the ball from his teammates in his desire to take a penalty.

The second penalty of the game was taken by Ronaldo, who lifted his season's total to nine and delighted Barcelona fans shocked by news of a reported $34 million bid for the Brazilian star from Italian giants AC Milan.
The result also put to rest worries by the return to form of arch rivals Real Madrid, 6-1 winners over Real Sociedad.
In another game played on Saturday John Toshack's Deportivo kept up with the pace with a 2-0 win over Espanyol.

A further point back on 17 are Real Betis, who maintained their challenge in the 3-0 home win over Rayo Vallecano with three fine goals from Spanish internationals Alfonso Perez and Pier Cherubino and former Ajax striker George Finidi.
Reigning champions Atletico showed their character despite losing at last year's runners-up, Valencia.

The match began at a tremedous pace, and was just five minutes old when Atletico's Juan Eduardo Esnaider forced an amazing one-handed save from Valencia's Andoni Zubizarreta after a superb move down the right by Milinko Pantic and Kiko Narvaez.
Moments later the veteran keeper was beaten by a corner which bounced off the bar by set-piece specialist Milinko Pantic.
But Valencia withstood the pressure, and went ahead after 36 minutes when Antonio Poyatos scored a diving header from a cross by Enrique Romero.
Shortly afterwards Atletico's Juan Lopez left his side with 10 men after picking up a second yellow card.
After the restart Kiko missed a simple chance to equalise, and Valencia made the champions pay for it when Croatian striker Goran Vlaovic finished off a fine move by Gabriel Moya.
Esnaider pulled one back for Atletico in the final minutes of an end-to-end game before Claudio Lopez sealed the match with a superb 45 metre lob over Atletico keeper Jose Molina.

After a poor start marred by problems with Brazilian striker Romario, who is still in Brazil, Valencia have moved into contention and are now in seventh place with 13 points. Atletico are two points back in ninth.
